article.headline: Hot 5-1 Philadelphia 76ers storm Spectrum Center to face struggling Charlotte Hornets
article.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers face the Charlotte Hornets at the Spectrum Center on Saturday night in an Eastern Conference NBA matchup.
article.body:
Tyrese Maxey enters the matchup averaging more than 28 points per game, spearheading a Philadelphia offense that has surged to a 5-1 record. The 76ers arrive in Charlotte following a gritty 98-93 victory over the New York Knicks on Friday night, marking their fourth win in five games.

This Saturday night clash carries significant implications for the Eastern Conference standings as Philadelphia looks to maintain its championship momentum. For the Charlotte Hornets, the game represents a critical opportunity to regain footing after enduring back-to-back losses against the Detroit Pistons and Washington Wizards. With the 76ers playing on the second night of a back-to-back, the Hornets aim to leverage home-court advantage at the Spectrum Center to disrupt Philadelphia's rhythm.

According to Yahoo Sports, Charlotte relies heavily on Brandon Miller, who is currently averaging more than 24 points per game. However, the Hornets face depth challenges due to recent injuries affecting their supporting cast. To secure a win, Charlotte must execute a high-level defensive game plan and maintain efficient scoring against a Philadelphia roster anchored by the paint dominance of Joel Embiid. Both teams are navigating the fatigue of consecutive nights of play.

The game is scheduled to tip off at 6 p.m. ET. Fans can watch the live broadcast on NBA TV, with additional streaming options available through platforms like Fubo for those looking to follow the action in real time.

article.headline: Jaylen Brown remains questionable for Sixers matchup against the Charlotte Hornets tonight
article.summary: Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown is listed as questionable for Saturday's road game against the Charlotte Hornets due to left patellar tendinopathy.
article.body: Jaylen Brown’s availability for the Philadelphia 76ers remains uncertain as the team prepares for the second leg of a back-to-back road trip. The forward, who is dealing with left patellar tendinopathy, was listed as questionable in the team’s official injury report released Saturday afternoon following his absence during Friday’s win over the New York Knicks. Brown previously reported soreness in his left knee following a 114-109 victory against the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse has stated that the timetable for Brown’s return depends on his ongoing treatment and pain tolerance, noting that there is no long-term concern regarding the injury. Through his first five games this season, Brown has averaged 20.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 4.2 assists. The status of other key roster members adds to the uncertainty for the Sixers in Charlotte. While LeBron James and Joel Embiid are officially ruled out for tonight’s game due to injury management, the team may see the return of Jabari Walker from a knee injury. Additionally, center Tacko Fall is listed as questionable and could potentially make his season debut. The Sixers enter this contest coming off a 98-93 victory on Friday night. The organization will continue to monitor Brown’s condition leading up to tip-off against the Hornets as they navigate a busy schedule that includes upcoming NBA Cup group stage matchups against the Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat, and Indiana Pacers throughout November.

article.headline: Second Storm System Brings Widespread Flood Risk Across Arizona This Weekend
article.summary: Phoenix will see rain chances increase Saturday night through Sunday as a second storm system moves through the region.
article.body:
Residents across Arizona should prepare for a long-duration rain event that arrives Saturday night and continues through Sunday. While Saturday begins with quiet, partly cloudy conditions, moisture will push into the region by the evening, bringing widespread rainfall that is expected to continue through the following day. This secondary storm system follows an initial round of thunderstorms that triggered a flood warning for the northeast Valley and Maricopa County.

A flood watch covers most of Arizona from Saturday night through Monday morning, highlighting a persistent risk of flooding in urban areas, canyons, and low water crossings. Because this event involves on-and-off rain for several hours, water accumulation could occur even if the individual storms are not considered severe. Drivers and residents in low-lying areas should remain alert as river levels are expected to rise to flood stage in certain spots.

Temperatures in Phoenix are expected to drop throughout the weekend, with a high of 78 degrees on Saturday followed by a high of 70 degrees on Sunday. According to AZ Family and FOX 10 Phoenix, the rain will begin to move out of the area by Sunday evening, though lingering showers may persist in eastern Arizona into Monday morning. The start of the workweek should remain quiet in Phoenix as drier air moves into the region. For those planning outdoor activities, trick-or-treat hours are currently expected to be dry for most of the state before the moisture arrives.

news.title: Turismo nautico Sicilia: 1.712 imprese, posti barca record
news.og_title: Turismo nautico Sicilia: 1.712 imprese, posti barca record
news.og_desc: Al Seacily di Castellammare del Golfo è stato presentato il report di Assonautica Palermo e Otie sul turismo nautico in Sicilia. Le imprese della filiera risalgono a 1.712 nel primo trimestre 2026 dopo il calo a 1.671 del 2025. Il refit è l'unico comparto in crescita costante e vale il 35,6% dei 6.239 addetti. I posti barca toccano il record di 17.914, le nuove patenti sono 1.887, seconda regione in Italia. Il charter dipende per il 61-80% dalla clientela internazionale ma non è integrato con le filiere locali.
